project.name: Pillarwatch
project.goal: A self-hosted status page that shows the up/down history of a small team's own services, no third-party dependency.
project.primary_user: An on-call engineer at a small team who wants an honest status page without paying for or trusting a SaaS status vendor.
project.core_problem: Small teams either run no status page (users find out about outages from support tickets) or hand uptime data to a third-party SaaS that is one more thing to trust and pay for.
project.core_journey:
1. The team registers a service with a health-check URL.
2. Pillarwatch polls it on an interval and records up/down transitions.
3. A public page renders current status and a 90-day history bar per service.
project.success_measure: A service outage shows up on the public page within one poll interval of the health check failing, with no manual step.
project.success_metrics:
- time from real outage to page reflecting it -- under one poll interval
- self-hosted install time -- under 10 minutes on a single binary
project.riskiest_assumption: A simple interval poll plus a small state machine (up/down/degraded) is enough signal for a small team, without needing synthetic transactions or multi-region checks.
project.req_ac_list:
- [ ] **REQ-AC1:** A registered service that fails its health check flips to "down" and the public page reflects it within one poll interval.
- [ ] **REQ-AC2:** A service that recovers flips back to "up" and the incident is closed with a duration.
- [ ] **REQ-AC3:** The public page renders a 90-day history bar per service from stored transitions.
project.non_goals:
- No multi-region or synthetic-transaction checks.
- No paging/alerting integrations in the first cut -- the page itself is the notification.
project.other_users: - End users of the team's product, checking whether an outage is known (read-only, no login).
project.constraint_time: One weekend project; first usable cut in a few evenings.
project.constraint_cost: Must run as a single small binary on a $5/month VM; no managed database requirement.
project.constraint_data: Health-check results and incident history only; no user accounts or personal data collected from the public page.
project.deployment_target: A single Linux VM, reverse-proxied behind the team's existing domain.
project.scale_expectations: Under 50 registered services, polled every 30-60 seconds; a handful of concurrent public-page viewers during an incident.
project.integrations:
- Outbound HTTP health checks against each registered service's URL.
- Optional outbound webhook on status change (stretch goal, not in the first cut).
project.in_scope_list:
- Service registration with a health-check URL and poll interval.
- Poller with an up/down/degraded state machine and transition history.
- Public status page with current status and a 90-day history bar per service.
project.pain_point: no honest status page without paying for or trusting a SaaS vendor
project.current_alternative: a paid third-party status-page SaaS, or no status page at all
project.key_benefit: an honest, self-hosted status page with no third party in the loop
project.key_differentiator: single-binary self-hosted install instead of a hosted SaaS subscription

positive_reference.ref: the single-binary, no-frills operational feel of Uptime Kuma

design.references:
- Uptime Kuma -- calm, information-dense status list that stays legible mid-incident
- Basecamp's status page -- plain, confident typography with zero marketing chrome
design.anti_reference: a marketing-site status page: hero banner, gradient background, animated illustrations distracting from the actual up/down signal

features.title: Register a service and start polling it
features.intent: A team can register a service with a health-check URL and poll interval, and the poller starts checking it.
features.serves: journey step 1: the team registers a service with a health-check URL
acceptance: A newly registered service is polled at its configured interval and its first result is recorded.

features.title: Public status page shows current status and history
features.intent: The public page renders each service's current status and a 90-day history bar from stored transitions.
features.serves: REQ-AC3: the public page renders a 90-day history bar per service from stored transitions
acceptance: The public page shows every registered service's current status and a 90-day history bar built from its recorded transitions.
